name: Sri Lankan Soya Curry
steps: Cover dry soya chunks with 900 ml boiling water and soak 12 minutes. Drain, rinse well and squeeze out excess water; this removes the packaged taste and lets the chunks absorb curry.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan. Cook onion 6 minutes until golden, then add garlic, ginger, chilies, curry leaves and cinnamon for 1 minute.
Stir in curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds, then tomato. Cook 5–6 minutes until the tomato collapses and oil separates from the spice base.
Add squeezed soya chunks and toss 3 minutes to coat. Pour in 180 ml water and coconut milk, add salt, and simmer uncovered 12–15 minutes until the chunks are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Remove cinnamon, rest 5 minutes and serve with rice. Each chunk should be fully heated and saturated with the spiced coconut gravy.
tips: Squeeze the rehydrated chunks thoroughly; otherwise the curry can taste watery and the sauce will not penetrate.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
